knowledge_units.context_summary: The study analyzes radio properties of EGRET-detected blazars using the VLBA Imaging and Polarimetry Survey (VIPS), which has a flux limit roughly an order of magnitude lower than the MOJAVE survey. At these lower flux levels, radio flux density does not directly correlate with gamma-ray flux density, though EGRET blazars exhibit higher brightness temperatures, greater core fractions, and larger jet opening angles. These trends are attributed to systematically larger Doppler factors in gamma-ray loud blazars, consistent with higher apparent velocities observed at radio frequencies above 10 GHz.

attributes.role: reference sample for EGRET blazar properties

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text reviews prior studies on the radio and polarization properties of EGRET blazars, noting conflicting results regarding jet velocities and compactness. It describes the completion of the 5 GHz VLBA Imaging and Polarimetry Survey (VIPS), which imaged 1127 flat-spectrum sources. The study defines a sample of 173 candidate EGRET sources by intersecting the EGRET catalog with the CRATES survey.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study analyzes 31 EGRET candidate blazars within the VIPS survey region, classifying them by morphology and comparing their properties to the broader VIPS population. The sample consists of 12 likely and 19 plausible candidates based on a Figure of Merit, with 6 sources also observed by MOJAVE. Morphological analysis reveals a higher proportion of long jets and a lack of compact symmetric objects compared to the general VIPS population.

Additionally, EGRET blazars exhibit higher polarization levels and are biased toward more core-dominated systems than the average VIPS source.

The distribution of jet lengths showed no appreciable difference between EGRET blazars and the VIPS population.
